historical_anchor.old_Type97_retrofit_note: About 300 older Type97 57mm tanks were rebuilt with Shinhoto turrets over the wartime transition; this is additional model-mix conversion, not new hull production.

strategic_allocation_logic: Early Malaya/Philippines/Burma success validates Japanese armored operations but does not remove IJN/IJA aviation priority.
Therefore national AFV output envelope stays near historical rather than exploding.
Branch advantage is used first to accelerate model transition, acceptance, recovery and divisional support.
Reliable Type95 performance makes an urgent KeNi switch less attractive.
Nomonhan + M3 experience makes 47mm Shinhoto/AT firepower more attractive than continued new-build 57mm medium tanks.

branch_1942_output_center.note: Center deliberately preserves the historical total production envelope. Mix is shifted, not national steel magically enlarged.

monthly_reconstructed_new_build.archive_guard: These are event-timing model curves, not archival monthly production values.

Shinhoto_retrofit_existing_hulls.interpretation: Branch front-loads most of the historically attested rebuild program. Remaining ~50-ish historical-equivalent rebuilds can close in 1943 after gun/turret ledger check.

Shinhoto_total_additions_1942.important: Only 525 are new physical hulls. 178 are already-existing Type97s moved from 57mm to 47mm category.

Type1_47mm_AT_and_tank_gun_gate.reason: Tank guns and towed AT guns share bore/ammunition/arsenal ecosystem but exact annual gun split is not securely established.
Type1_47mm_AT_and_tank_gun_gate.rule: The 525 new turrets + 178 retrofit turrets are provisional until Osaka Arsenal gun/turret output confirms this throughput. If gun output is lower, retrofit volume is the first item to slide, not new hull production already contracted.

ChiHe_1942.logic: Branch can close welding/240hp-engine/design loops faster, but successful Shinhoto makes a crash line conversion irrational while national priority is naval/air.

HoNiI_1942.source_of_delta: slightly earlier evaluation closure and armored-division artillery demand
HoNiI_1942.resource_guard: extra units consume Type97 chassis and Type90 75mm gun resources; no larger expansion until artillery gun ledger.

KeNi_1942.diverted_capacity: repair/recovery/tractor/special AFV work rather than extra medium tanks
KeNi_1942.logic: A more reliable Ha-Go strengthens the same historical reason Ke-Ni was low priority.

Philippines.branch_candidate: A small earlier replacement batch can be sent from the prewar accepted pool; exact 4th/7th Regiment issue and shipping must be event-audited before changing battles.
Philippines.historical_anchor: Two Shinhoto were present for Corregidor after complaints about the 57mm gun.

Malaya.policy: No automatic conversion of the 1st Tank Regiment before campaign end. 57mm HE remains useful against infantry/positions and the British lack a large local tank force.

Burma.policy: 47mm AT guns and limited Shinhoto reinforcement are potentially valuable against Stuart-equipped British armor, but must pass Rangoon/road/shipping allocation.

Manchuria_China.priority: Major recipient of new Shinhoto as tank divisions form in Manchuria and the 3rd Tank Division forms in China.

end_1942_consequence.core: The Japanese medium-tank fleet is much more rapidly 47mm-heavy than in a simple historical deployment reading, without increasing the national hull wallet much.
not_granted: automatic Shinhoto presence in every Southern Army tank regiment

next_gate: Reconstruct 1943: 427 Shinhoto new, Chi-He 15 historical, Ho-Ni II 14, Ka-Mi 112, tank divisions and Branch Five operation demand.
Then audit 1942 Southern battles only where dated replacement shipments materially change vehicle mix.
